jobs.occupation: 1352 Postdoctoral position in marine ecological modelling
jobs.description:
About the Position
The Institute of Marine Research (IMR) offers a 3-year postdoctoral position as part of the MORSE (“Models supporting practical restoration of habitats and species in Europe’s seas”) research project funded by Horizon Europe. This project sits within IMR’s strategic initiative to build a strong center for marine research within one of Europe's largest marine research institutes. The candidate will ideally start in early 2027. 

We seek a postdoctoral researcher with a background in ecological modelling, with relevant experience and publication record on modelling marine and/or aquatic ecosystems. The postdoctoral researcher will work across several work packages, including WP5 (reviewing and compiling data on restoration pathways, pressures, and ecological needs of focal species and habitats, and defining favourable reference areas), WP6 (species distribution modelling and assessment of environmental status (NEAT), WP7 (modelling land-, and sea-based pressures, and MPAs), and WP8 (modelling ecosystem services). The broader aim of the project is to develop and demonstrate effective and climate-resilient restoration models for European marine ecosystems to inform more effective restoration efforts. 

The postdoctoral researcher will work with a team of researchers at IMR and collaborating partners to carry out and deliver research outcomes in the MORSE project. The MORSE project that the postdoctoral position is associated with is a 4-year project that is led by the Finnish Environmental Institute (SYKE) and includes institutions across seven European countries (Finland, Sweden, Norway, UK, Spain, Portugal, and Greece). Travel to workshops and meetings in these countries should be anticipated. The postdoctoral researcher will gain mentoring support, training, and networking opportunities from the leading researchers associated with the MORSE project, and have the opportunity to establish connections and advance their research career over the course of the project. More information about MORSE can be found at the project website: https://morse-project.eu/ 

Knowledge about northern European marine ecosystems is an advantage, as the postdoctoral researcher will be responsible for modelling Norwegian marine ecosystems. The position is placed within the Benthic Communities research group and can be located at any of the IMR offices. Note that the IMR project lead (Karine Gagnon) is based at Flødevigen Research Station, but the research group includes members across all three locations. IMR has good links and cooperation with industry, management, and the university sector. We offer the opportunity to be part of a collaborative, interdisciplinary, and ambitious research group with strong national and international links.

Main tasks:

• Lead and support MORSE research activities as directed by project leaders. 
• Write research publications, reports, and grant proposals.
• Participate in scientific conferences, science communication, and outreach activities. 
• Review and compile existing data on restoration pathways, ecosystem status, and pressures for focal species and habitats, and define favourable reference areas for these 
• Review and compile existing models and data sources for the Norwegian sea areas (including the Skagerrak, Norwegian Sea, North Sea, and Barents Sea) 
• Apply species distribution models and assess environmental status using the NEAT tool 
• Model land-based and sea-based pressures on marine habitats, and the role of MPAs 
• Model climate scenarios and ecosystem services 
• Participate in work package coordination and reporting 
• Maintain and curate datasets and coordinate data sharing and modelling efforts across MORSE partners.About the Research Group and Our Work
The Benthic Communities group focuses on research, mapping, and monitoring of benthic ecosystems, including seagrass meadows, macroalgae forests, and deep-sea ecosystems. Research within the project will support IMR’s national advisory task on ecosystem-based management of seas and coastal areas, where environmental changes and human activities and are important factors. The research group has over 30 employees base on Flødevigen, Bergen, and Tromsø.
Qualification Requirements
For this position, we are looking for a candidate with

• PhD in biology or ecology, preferably with a focus on ecological modelling
• Documented experience in ecological modelling 
• Strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and oral skills in English
The working language at the Institute of Marine Research is Norwegian. Being able to communicate well in Norwegian is an important prerequisite for both the employee and our institute. We expect non-Norwegian-speaking employees to complete Norwegian language courses during the first two years of employment. The institute will cover the cost of completed and passed Norwegian courses.
Personal Qualities
At the Institute of Marine Research, we believe that personality plays a role in how one works, communicates, and thrives in the workplace. For this position, we are looking for a colleague who

• Good communication and collaboration skills. 
• Good organisational and logistics skills. 
• Ability to complete work on time and meeting deadline 
• Ability to work efficiently independently and in teams.Desired Qualifications
• Strong skills and experience in ecological modelling and data analysis
• Ability and willingness to collaborate with colleagues in Norway and abroad 
• Ability and willingness to organize and lead joint modelling efforts with partners abroad 
• Research experience in marine ecosystems, species, and habitats 
• Research experience in ecological restoration and/or conservationInclusion and Diversity is a Strength
The Institute of Marine Research believes that inclusion and diversity are strengths. Therefore, we encourage all qualified candidates to apply for a position with us, regardless of age, gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic background. The Institute is an Inclusive Workplace (IA) company, and we aim to accommodate applicants with disabilities.

If there are qualified applicants with disabilities, employment gaps, or immigrant backgrounds, we will invite at least one applicant from each of these groups to an interview. To be considered for affirmative action, you must meet the requirements and indicate that you wish to be considered for the action in your application. You can read more here.
Your application must include 
• a cover letter describing your research interests and motivation for applying for the position. The letter should not exceed one A4 page.• Full name and contact details for two or three referees, preferably your PhD supervisor and/or references from recent employment.• CV, transcripts, diplomas, and relevant certificates.• A list of scientific publications, if applicable.

All documents must be in a Scandinavian language or in English. Candidates with documentation from foreign institutions must include an explanation of the institution’s grading system.
We offer
• the opportunity to work in one of Europe’s leading marine research institutes
• a creative working environment
• facilities in either Flødevigen, Bergen or Tromsø 
• flexible work hours 
• public sector occupational pension through the Norwegian Public Service Pension Funds (SPK)
• access to company cabins, fitness facilities, and other welfare benefitsAditional information
The position is remunerated as 1352 Postdoctoral in accordance with the main collective agreement in the state sector, depending on your qualifications and the characteristics of the position. A 2 % contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted from the salary.

Applications must be submitted electronically via Jobbnorge.

Please note that information about applicants may be made public even if the applicant has requested not to be listed. Applicants will be informed in advance if such disclosure is necessary.

The Institute of Marine Research is subject to export control regulations. These regulations apply to the processing of applications for the position.

Applicants with education from abroad may be asked to provide NOKUT approval of their qualifications. You may be asked to approve that the Institute of Marine Research conducts a background check.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The Institute of Marine Research is one of Europe’s largest marine research institutes, with over 1,000 employees and a range of high-standard research facilities and laboratories. Our main activities are research, advisory work, and monitoring. The institute owns and operates eight research vessels. Our headquarters are in Bergen, with additional offices in Tromsø and research stations in Matre, Austevoll, and Flødevigen.The Institute of Marine Research aims to be a leading provider of knowledge to ensure the sustainable management of marine ecosystem resources—nationally and internationally—across the entire value chain from ocean to food, including the marine environment, fish nutrition, and safe, healthy seafood.

About the Job

The Embassy of Israel to Norway and Iceland is seeking a dedicated, highly responsible, and vigilant Security Officer. The primary responsibility of this role is to ensure the safety, security, and physical protection of embassy personnel, visitors, assets, and premises.

Working as a key member of the embassy's security team, you will be responsible for maintaining a safe and secure working environment, implementing security protocols, and managing day-to-day access and incident response.

Central Tasks Include, but are not limited to:

● Personnel & Facility Safety: Ensure the physical security and protection of all embassy staff, diplomats, visitors, and premises.

● Surveillance & Monitoring: Oversee security systems, CCTV, alarm systems, and physical entry points to detect and mitigate potential security threats.

● Incident Response & Risk Assessment: Respond swiftly to security alerts or incidents, and perform regular risk assessments of the premises and official events.

● Coordination with Local Authorities: Maintain professional communication and coordination with local Norwegian law enforcement, emergency services, and security partners.

● Event & Visit Security: Assist in planning and executing security measures for official embassy events, delegations, and high-level visits.

Qualifications and Experience

● Relevant background or experience in security, law enforcement, military service, or a closely related field.

● Knowledge of physical security principles, access control systems, and risk management.

● Excellent communication skills in both Norwegian and English.

● High level of physical fitness, discretion, and reliability.

Personal Characteristics

● Highly responsible, observant, and calm under pressure.

● Strong decision-making skills with a proactive approach to threat detection and problem-solving.

● Exceptional integrity, professionalism, and strict adherence to confidentiality.

● Excellent teamwork and interpersonal skills.

● A strong commitment to ensuring the safety and well-being of embassy staff and operations.

Application Details

● Salary: Determined based on background and experience.

● Application Process: Please submit your CV and a short cover letter to: cso@oslo.mfa.gov.il

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in Political Science - Norway and the EU
jobs.description:
About the position 
ARENA Centre for European Studies at the University of Oslo invites applications for a position as PhD Research Fellow (SKO 1017) in political science or another relevant social science discipline. The position is for a period of three years, with no teaching or other required duties. 

The place of work is ARENA Centre for European Studies, University of Oslo.
 
ARENA is an interdisciplinary research centre at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo. Since 1994, the centre has studied political, security, economic, legal and social integration, transformation and cooperation in Europe. ARENA has extensive experience in coordinating international research projects and networks funded by European and Norwegian institutions. 

The centre has around 30 academic and four administrative staff. More information about ARENA is available here.
More about the position 
Europe is being reshaped by war, geopolitical rivalry and a renewed enlargement agenda. As the EU's rules and decisions reach further beyond its borders, Norway faces key questions about alignment, influence and democratic control. Norway is one of the most closely integrated non-member states. That makes it an important case for understanding what it means to be part of European integration without being a member of the Union.

ARENA is looking for a PhD Research Fellow who wants to write a dissertation on Norway's relationship with the EU. The successful candidate will develop and carry out their own doctoral project in a research environment with long experience of studying European integration and its consequences for countries both inside and outside the Union.

We expect theoretically informed empirical studies and particularly welcome projects that take a comparative approach, but single-case studies of Norway are also welcome. Examples of comparisons could include comparing and contrasting Norway with other associated or third countries (such as Iceland, Switzerland or the United Kingdom), EU member states or candidate countries. Comparisons across policy areas are also welcome. We are open to a range of theoretical and methodological approaches.

Relevant research areas could include, but are not limited to:

• Norway's association model: Projects could for example address how the EEA Agreement and Norway's many other agreements with the EU shape Norwegian politics, public administration and regulation, or how they compare with those of comparable EU member or affiliated states. Projects could look at Norway's room for manoeuvre and influence vis-à-vis the EU, at questions of democratic legitimacy and control, or at how the association model is evolving as the EU changes. 
• Justice and home affairs: Projects could for example address Norway's participation in Schengen, European migration and asylum policy, border management, or police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. Projects could study how EU developments in these fields affect Norwegian policies, institutions and societal security, possibly compared with other associated or member countries.
We are looking for candidates with interesting and relevant research ideas, strong theoretical and analytical skills, and solid methodological competence. The project proposal should combine clear theoretical and empirical ambitions with a realistic and feasible research design.
Responsibilities
The appointment as a PhD Research Fellow at ARENA is for a period of three years, with no compulsory duties. As a fellow, you will be based at ARENA Centre for European Studies’ premises in Gaustadalléen, Oslo. Presence at the unit is a requirement. 

You will be admitted to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo.

This is a full-time position commencing in the winter or spring of 2027. You will have access to office space, equipment, and services, as well as resources for fieldwork and conference participation as needed.
What skills are important in this role?
Required selection criteria 

• The position requires a completed master's degree equivalent to a two-year programme (120 ECTS credits) within the social sciences, approved by the faculty as a basis for admission.
• Grades placing the candidate in the top tier of the field (this also applies to the master's thesis)
• The master's degree must include relevant training in research design and methodology
• The master's thesis must correspond to a minimum workload of six months, i.e., 30 ECTS credits
• 
Excellent oral and written English proficiency is required

ARENA’s working language is English, and therefore, fluency in oral and written English is required. As Norway’s relationship with the EU is central to the position, Norwegian sources will be important, making good proficiency in Norwegian (or another Scandinavian language) an advantage.
 
Personal suitability

• You must be able to work independently and in a structured manner.

• You should possess good collaborative skills and demonstrate the ability, willingness, and commitment to contribute to the development of the research field.

• 
You should be able to take initiative and wish to participate actively in an international and interdisciplinary research team.

Appointment as a research fellow requires admission to a doctoral programme, or a binding agreement regarding admission. 

Application for admission to a PhD programme must normally be submitted within three months of the start of the research project leading to the PhD degree. 
Basis for assessment
In the assessment of candidates, particular emphasis will be placed on:

(1) the quality and relevance of the project proposal

(2) academic qualifications (transcripts must be attached)

(3) the master's thesis and any other published work

(4) references.

Personal qualities and motivation will be taken into consideration.

Potential candidates will be invited to an interview.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

Efficient boiling and condensation are fundamental to thermal management in refrigeration, air conditioning, electronics cooling and energy systems. The candidate will investigate how interfacial transport and surface characteristics can be represented reliably in numerical simulations and will validate modelling approaches against experimental evidence generated within the network. 

The successful candidate will work at at the Thermal Two-Phase Flow Laboratory (http://folk.ntnu.no/fernandi/) at NTNU’s main Gløshaugen campus in Trondheim, Norway. Numerical simulations will be performed on both commercial packages and with in-house developed numerical codes. The candidate will be part of a friendly working environment, with close interaction with our postdoc, PhD and MSc candidates working in our group. The position will be supervised by Professor Maria Fernandino.

About the position
We invite applications for a full time permanent position as Associate Professor in Clincal Pharmacy at the Section for Pharmaceutics and Social Pharmacy, Department of Pharmacy, University of Oslo.
About the Department and what we are looking for in this position
The Department of Pharmacy at the University of Oslo is seeking a highly motivated, dynamic, and innovative researcher with strong collaborative and educational skills. The Department has a strong interdisciplinary environment that covers the key areas of the pharmaceutical field. Cutting-edge research, extensive national and international collaboration, and an integrated Master’s programme in Pharmacy position the Department as a key contributor to the development of pharmacy in Norway. We place strong emphasis on collaboration with the healthcare sector, regulatory authorities, as well as the pharmaceutical industry. The Section for Pharmaceutics and Social pharmacy is one of the three sections at the Department of Pharmacy and is comprised of strong research groups specializing in clinical pharmacy, as well as pharmacoepidemiology and pharmaceutics. The section offers an active and dynamic academic environment, ideal for ambitious researchers. The research environment (Clinical pharmacy - Department of Pharmacy) focuses on patient safety, medication use, and continuity of care, supported by methodological expertise spanning from qualitative studies to randomised trials, as well as health care innovation and strong collaboration with healthcare partners in the Oslo region.
 
The life science environment in the Oslo region is developing steadily, supported by collaboration between the pharmaceutical sector, the university hospital and hospital pharmacy, and academic institutions. Oslo Science City and the new Life Science Building are central initiatives contributing to this development. The Department of Pharmacy is relocating to the new Life Science Building in 2026 (Life Science building- UiO:Livsvitenskap). This move will provide modern facilities designed to strengthen research, teaching, and collaboration across the health and life science disciplines at the University of Oslo. 

The ideal candidate will play an important role in shaping the department’s activities in the new Life Science Building by contributing to the development of pharmaceutical sciences within a strong interdisciplinary environment. In particular, the candidate is expected to strengthen research and academic activity to contribute to the research group’s collaboration with healthcare partners and other research groups. Documented experience with interdisciplinary work and international cooperation is highly desirable.

The successful candidate should have documented independent research experience in addition to the PhD degree with publications in international peer review journals. Furthermore, the candidate should have a documented history of securing significant external funding, or at least strong funding application efforts.  
Your main tasks will be
• Teaching and supervision, mainly in social pharmacy, at all levels of the five-years study program in pharmacy, including master- and PhD. 
• Course leadership for the main course in social pharmacy at the undergraduate program.
• Initiating and conducting high quality research within the research group’s focus areas, including contributing to external funding.
• Contributing to the development of a strong and sustainable research group.
• Carrying out examination related duties and contributing to academic administration as required. More information about the position
Applicants must document academic qualifications in their field, equivalent to an Associate professor position. The successful applicant must be able to teach at all levels and to supervise Master and PhD students. The successful applicant may furthermore be required to take on other teaching duties and administrative tasks, by request from the Department or the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences. 
What skills are important in this role?
Required qualifications that must be documented in the application::

• The successful applicant must have completed a PhD preferably in clinical or social pharmacy and have a strong scientific track record within the area.
• Master’s degree in pharmacy or equivalent must be formally documented. 
• Scientific qualifications will play a major role, with main emphasis placed on research output from the last five years. 
• Documented potential for further acquisition of external funding.
• Documented knowledge of Scandinavian pharmaceutical practice and traditions.
• Pedagogical qualifications and teaching and supervision experience at all levels will be an important factor in the evaluation process and should be well documented in a teaching portfolio. The applicant should describe her/his qualifications in view of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) framework which includes:
• Focus on student learning
• A clear development over time

jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of Geography and Social Anthropology offers a PhD Candidate position for a period of three years.The Department of Geography and Social Anthropology invites candidates to apply for a three-year position as a PhD Research Fellow in Geography with focus on Post-Fossil Fuel Transitions in Petroleum-Producing Nations. The PhD fellow will be part of the Research Group “Geographies of Just and Sustainable Transitions”, and will join a dynamic and collegial research environment that includes both early career and senior researchers working across a broad range of fields at the Department.The PhD fellow will also be affiliated with the NTNU Strategic Area on Energy under the focus area “Beyond the Fossil Fuel Era” and will be supervised by Alexander Dodge and co-supervised by Amber Nordholm and Espen Moe.Starting date as soon as possible/by agreement.Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The global oil and gas (O&G) sector sits at a critical conjuncture – there is broad consensus among governments, industry and market outlooks that global oil demand will plateau or peak between 2030 and 2035 as governments around the world work to meet their climate commitments and as new technologies (i.e. solar panels, heat pumps, batteries, etc.) gain traction in global markets. At the same time, however, the pace and speed of fossil fuel decline afterwards is highly uncertain. The Strait of Hormuz blockades have generated enormous revenue for O&G companies but may also prove to be an inflection point that accelerates efforts to move beyond fossil fuels. The uncertainty surrounding the future of fossil fuels is particularly prevalent for governments in petroleum-producing nations. On one hand, governments are under increasing pressure by the public and civil society organizations to end fossil fuel subsidies, stop new field exploration and development, and transition their economies away from fossil-fuel production. On the other hand, as the energy transition progresses, it has created its own counterforces and resulted in political pushback from climate-skeptical or even climate-denying political populists who have argued that the energy transition is inefficient, expensive, and unduly harming regular people, and that the only thing that protects the economy and preserves the welfare state is to open new areas for exploration and to provide tax relief/subsidies to stimulate new developments.The primary objective of the PhD project should be to investigate and better understand the contradictions and dilemmas democratic states in petroleum-producing nations must negotiate and navigate through uncertainty surrounding the direction and pace of transition to a post-fossil fuel era. Drawing energy geographies, (cultural) political economy and/or sustainability transitions, the successful candidate should examine the politics, strategies, counterforces, and/or backlashes surrounding statecraft in democratic petroleum-producing nations. This entails a focus on the role of and relationships between institutional legacies, vested interests, labor, expertise (consultants, think-tanks, academia, etc.) and/or civil society in shaping how the democratic-states conducts public affairs, initiates government projects, and manages domestic and international relations surrounding the petroleum-sector and fossil-fuel transitions.Successful candidates may choose to limit their study to the Norwegian-context or conduct a cross-comparative study between Norway and other democratic petroleum-producing nations such as United Kingdom, Indonesia, and Australia. Candidates should aim to contribute to discussions in national newspapers or public forums that could eventually feed into discussions surrounding the report from Norway’s Transition Commission (“Omstillingskommisjon”).
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Be a part of the Just and Sustainable Transition research group at the Department of Geography.
• Help organize events for the Beyond Fossil Fuel Focus Area at NTNU Energy
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions.Be prepared for changes to your work duties during the employment period.Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the PhD Programme in Social Sciences with Specialization in Geography at NTNU, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• Your education must be equivalent to a five-year Norwegian degree.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in Human Geography, Science and Technology Studies, Political Science or an equivalent degree in Social Sciences. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English
• Experience with Qualitative Research Methodologies in Social Science
• High-quality research proposals and a research plan that is relevant for the project and existing research at the department and among the supervisors.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Relevance of a professional background
• Experience with quantitative methods/social network analysis is a plus.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian equivalent level B2Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity 
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Social Sciences with Specialization in Geography within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

About the application

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

In addition, applicants are required to answer the position-related screening questions in Jobbnorge when submitting their application.If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information

If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Associate Professor Alexander Dodge, +47 73591911, alexander.dodge@ntnu.no. If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Advisor Renate Lillian Johansen e-mail: renate.johansen@ntnu.no.
